units.function: PostgreSQL integration tests for resolving a human responsibleUserId before a Heartbeat run is created.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises heartbeatService against Company, membership, Issue, Agent, wakeup and Run persistence while mocking only adapter execution.
units.keyDataModels: Company.defaultResponsibleUserId, Issue.responsibleUserId, HeartbeatRun.responsibleUserId, triggering actor identity and active Company membership.
units.lifecycle: Issue-scoped automation uses the Issue responsible user; manual runs use the triggering user; ownerless system work falls back to the Company default; Issue creator is never treated as implicit responsibility; unresolved responsibility rejects with structured code before Run creation.
units.testAssessment: Six focused integration cases validate the precedence and fail-closed behavior, including the critical no-Run side-effect assertion. Coverage does not prove the selected human is active, authorized for the exact action/data contract, notified, or accountable through approval and result acceptance.
units.designRationale: Separate authorship and triggering from ongoing human responsibility, and prevent autonomous execution when no responsible human can be named.
units.companyOsProblem: This is directly aligned with Company OS: every executable Work must bind an accountable human before dispatch, independent of Agent vendor or requester.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as a stronger ResponsibilityContract resolution gate. Require active human principal, organization/role authority, execution/data/approval contract digests and a versioned resolution receipt; keep the stable responsible_user_unresolved-style code and no-side-effect failure invariant.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip records a responsible user but does not establish that person's acceptance, authority scope or liability for a particular Work action. A Company-level default is too broad to become silent authorization.

units.function: PostgreSQL tests for eliminating phantom queued/running Runs when an execution-environment lease is released.
units.dependencyDirection: Calls a Heartbeat service terminalization helper over Run, Issue and Run-event tables; telemetry is mocked.
units.keyDataModels: HeartbeatRun status/errorCode, Issue terminal status, execution lease release and HeartbeatRunEvent.
units.lifecycle: On lease release, preserve an already terminal Run; otherwise mark it succeeded when its Issue is done, or interrupted with lease_released_before_terminal when the Issue remains non-terminal.
units.testAssessment: Five compact database cases cover queued/running, terminal/non-terminal Issue and already-terminal Run branches. They do not cover concurrent terminal writes, lease fencing tokens, multi-instance ownership, event publication atomicity or whether Issue done has valid result/evidence.
units.designRationale: The execution lease is a liveness boundary: releasing it must also close any stale live Run projection.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs fenced execution leases and deterministic terminalization so Agent Boss never sees a phantom live Agent after a Connector or local node releases capacity.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the invariant with a transactional Run ledger and outbox. Do not infer success from Work status alone: success requires the matching execution attempt, result/evidence receipt and responsibility contract; otherwise terminalize as interrupted or inconsistent for review.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip can convert a Run to succeeded solely because the Issue is done, even if another actor changed the Issue or evidence belongs to a different attempt.

units.function: Unit tests for sanitizing and bounding persisted Run-log chunks.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure Heartbeat helper tests with no database, adapter or UI dependencies.
units.keyDataModels: Untrusted Run-log text, inline base64 image bodies, credential-shaped values and bounded persisted chunks.
units.lifecycle: Redact inline image data and known credential shapes, then preserve a bounded head/tail representation with a truncation marker.
units.testAssessment: Three focused cases cover base64 image omission, truncation and several Paperclip credential shapes. Missing are streaming boundary splits, Unicode/encoding, adversarial near-matches, nested structured payloads, provider-specific secrets, property/fuzz tests and proof that sanitization precedes every sink.
units.designRationale: Reduce secret and binary-data retention while keeping enough terminal context for diagnosis.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS evidence and audit storage must be secret-safe, bounded and explicit about lossy transformation across every Connector.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as one defense inside a typed EvidenceSanitizationPort, with Connector-declared redaction rules, streaming-safe scanners, structured-field allowlists, content hashes, omission receipts and fuzz/fixture compatibility tests. Raw private reasoning must never enter the control plane.
units.responsibilityConflict: Regex-style post-processing of opaque logs cannot prove that production data, credentials or private reasoning were never persisted, and the truncation marker is brand/display text rather than a stable receipt code.

units.function: Unit tests for including canonical final assistant text in terminal realtime Run-status events while suppressing partial text for active Runs.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure event-payload helper tests over a Run-like object.
units.keyDataModels: Run status, resultJson.summary and live status event payload finalText.
units.lifecycle: Expose summary as finalText only after terminalization; emit null for a running attempt.
units.testAssessment: Two cases capture the core disclosure boundary but only test succeeded versus running. They omit failed/interrupted/cancelled outcomes, schema/version compatibility, result provenance, redaction, authorization and large/malformed payloads.
units.designRationale: Prevent partial model output from masquerading as a final answer while still delivering a terminal reply over realtime events.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs versioned progress and result events that clearly distinguish provisional output from accepted evidence-backed results.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the provisional-versus-final event distinction. Company OS should publish stable versioned ResultReceipt projections with attempt, evidence, authority and acceptance IDs rather than an untyped finalText field.
units.responsibilityConflict: Terminal status alone does not mean the text is approved, attributable, safe to disclose or accepted by the accountable human.
